# Use figspec with different R plotting systems

figspec works with figures made in ggplot2, lattice, grid, Plotly and
base R. Give
[`fig_save()`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/fig_save.md)
the editable figure or drawing code, and the same specification can
control its output size, resolution and format. Before writing the file,
figspec also applies the typography, line, colour and symbol settings
that the plotting system makes available.

The most complete workflow begins with an editable plot object or a base
R drawing function, while its instructions can still be adjusted. A
completed PNG or a recorded base plot contains less information about
how it was drawn, but figspec can still verify the properties recorded
in the finished file. Checking before and after export gives the fullest
account of the result.

## Use one specification with several plotting systems

The examples below use real observations from
[`ggplot2::mpg`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/mpg.html) and
the same project specification. The report requires a 110 × 75 mm PNG at
160 dpi, text between 9 and 11 points, and lines at least 0.6 points
wide. Its optional house style uses purple, amber and blue so the same
visual identity carries across each plotting system:

`figure_spec`` ``<-`` `[`list`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/list.html)`(`` `` name ``=`` ``"Shared research report"``,`` `` source_url ``=`` ``"internal:research-report-guide"``,`` `` verified_on ``=`` `[`as.character`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/character.html)`(`[`Sys.Date`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/Sys.time.html)`(``)``)``,`` `` columns ``=`` `[`list`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/list.html)`(``full ``=`` ``110``)``,`` `` formats ``=`` ``"png"``,`` `` dpi_min ``=`` ``160``,`` `` font_min_pt ``=`` ``9``,`` `` font_max_pt ``=`` ``11``,`` `` min_line_pt ``=`` ``0.6``,`` `` axis_lines_and_ticks ``=`` ``TRUE``,`` `` house_style ``=`` `[`list`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/list.html)`(`` `` palette ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``"#76549A"``, ``"#D99000"``, ``"#2B78A6"``)`` `` ``)`` ``)`` `` ``vehicle_data`` ``<-`` ``ggplot2``::`[`mpg`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/mpg.html)

The specification is an ordinary named R list. A registry profile such
as `"cell_press"` can be supplied in exactly the same position.

## ggplot2 and patchwork

For a ggplot2 figure, figspec can work with its layers, scales and
theme. It can apply the recorded typography and axis requirements, add
accessible colour and shape scales, control the data-panel dimensions
and inspect the editable plot as well as the completed file.

`ggplot_figure`` ``<-`` ``ggplot2``::`[`ggplot`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/ggplot.html)`(`` `` ``vehicle_data``,`` `` ``ggplot2``::`[`aes`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/aes.html)`(``displ``, ``hwy``, colour ``=`` ``drv``, shape ``=`` ``drv``)`` ``)`` ``+`` `` ``ggplot2``::`[`geom_point`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/geom_point.html)`(``size ``=`` ``1.8``, alpha ``=`` ``0.75``)`` ``+`` `` ``ggplot2``::`[`labs`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/labs.html)`(`` `` title ``=`` ``"Engine size and highway fuel economy"``,`` `` x ``=`` ``"Engine displacement (litres)"``,`` `` y ``=`` ``"Highway fuel economy"``,`` `` colour ``=`` ``"Drive type"``,`` `` shape ``=`` ``"Drive type"`` `` ``)`` `` ``ggplot_path`` ``<-`` `[`file.path`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/file.path.html)`(`[`tempdir`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/tempfile.html)`(``)``, ``"figspec-system-ggplot.png"``)`` ``ggplot_saved`` ``<-`` `[`fig_save`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/fig_save.md)`(`` `` ``ggplot_path``,`` `` ``ggplot_figure``,`` `` spec ``=`` ``figure_spec``,`` `` column ``=`` ``"full"``,`` `` height ``=`` ``75``,`` `` check ``=`` ``FALSE`` ``)`` ``summarise_export``(``ggplot_saved``)`` ``#> plotting_system requirements_applied canvas_mm`` ``#> 1 ggplot2 full 110 × 75`

![A scatter plot made with ggplot2 showing engine displacement and
highway fuel economy. Colour and shape distinguish drive
types.](data:image/png;base64,)

Patchwork compositions use the same
[`fig_save()`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/fig_save.md)
call. figspec applies the typography requirements across the component
plots and can set the size of each data panel. Patchwork continues to
control the arrangement.

## Base R graphics

Base R normally draws directly onto the active graphics device, so there
may be no plot object to hand to another function. Give figspec the
drawing code inside `function() { ... }` or a one-sided formula. figspec
can then open the correct device first and set its type size, font,
line-width and colour-palette defaults before the drawing runs.

`base_figure`` ``<-`` ``function``(``)`` ``{`` `` ``drive`` ``<-`` `[`factor`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/factor.html)`(``vehicle_data``$``drv``)`` `` ``graphics``::`[`plot`](https://rdrr.io/r/graphics/plot.default.html)`(`` `` ``vehicle_data``$``displ``,`` `` ``vehicle_data``$``hwy``,`` `` col ``=`` `[`as.integer`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/integer.html)`(``drive``)``,`` `` pch ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``16``, ``17``, ``15``)``[``drive``]``,`` `` xlab ``=`` ``"Engine displacement (litres)"``,`` `` ylab ``=`` ``"Highway fuel economy"``,`` `` main ``=`` ``"Engine size and highway fuel economy"`` `` ``)`` `` ``graphics``::`[`legend`](https://rdrr.io/r/graphics/legend.html)`(`` `` ``"topright"``,`` `` legend ``=`` `[`levels`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/levels.html)`(``drive``)``,`` `` col ``=`` `[`seq_along`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/seq.html)`(`[`levels`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/levels.html)`(``drive``)``)``,`` `` pch ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``16``, ``17``, ``15``)``,`` `` title ``=`` ``"Drive type"``,`` `` bty ``=`` ``"n"`` `` ``)`` ``}`` `` ``base_path`` ``<-`` `[`file.path`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/file.path.html)`(`[`tempdir`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/tempfile.html)`(``)``, ``"figspec-system-base.png"``)`` ``base_saved`` ``<-`` `[`fig_save`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/fig_save.md)`(`` `` ``base_path``,`` `` ``base_figure``,`` `` spec ``=`` ``figure_spec``,`` `` column ``=`` ``"full"``,`` `` height ``=`` ``75``,`` `` check ``=`` ``FALSE`` ``)`` ``summarise_export``(``base_saved``)`` ``#> plotting_system requirements_applied canvas_mm`` ``#> 1 base defaults 110 × 75`

![A scatter plot made with base R showing engine displacement and
highway fuel economy, exported through
figspec.](data:image/png;base64,)

The drawing function remains in control of values that it sets
explicitly. If the code requests 2-point text or a particular colour,
those instructions are used as written. Leave those values at their
defaults when you want figspec to supply them. A `recordedplot` can
still be exported and checked; use the drawing function when you also
want the specification applied before export.

## Lattice

A lattice plot is an editable `trellis` object. figspec supplies
specification- aware typography, colours, symbols, line types and line
widths through lattice settings, then prints the transformed object on
the requested device.

`if`` ``(`[`requireNamespace`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/ns-load.html)`(``"lattice"``, quietly ``=`` ``TRUE``)``)`` ``{`` `` ``lattice_figure`` ``<-`` ``lattice``::`[`xyplot`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/lattice/man/xyplot.html)`(`` `` ``hwy`` ``~`` ``displ``,`` `` data ``=`` ``vehicle_data``,`` `` groups ``=`` ``drv``,`` `` auto.key ``=`` `[`list`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/list.html)`(``space ``=`` ``"right"``, title ``=`` ``"Drive type"``)``,`` `` xlab ``=`` ``"Engine displacement (litres)"``,`` `` ylab ``=`` ``"Highway fuel economy"``,`` `` main ``=`` ``"Engine size and highway fuel economy"`` `` ``)`` `` `` ``lattice_path`` ``<-`` `[`file.path`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/file.path.html)`(`[`tempdir`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/tempfile.html)`(``)``, ``"figspec-system-lattice.png"``)`` `` ``lattice_saved`` ``<-`` `[`fig_save`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/fig_save.md)`(`` `` ``lattice_path``,`` `` ``lattice_figure``,`` `` spec ``=`` ``figure_spec``,`` `` column ``=`` ``"full"``,`` `` height ``=`` ``75``,`` `` check ``=`` ``FALSE`` `` ``)`` `` ``summarise_export``(``lattice_saved``)`` ``}`` ``#> plotting_system requirements_applied canvas_mm`` ``#> 1 lattice full 110 × 75`

![A lattice scatter plot of engine displacement and highway fuel
economy, with drive types distinguished by colour and
symbol.](data:image/png;base64,)

## Grid graphics

Grid figures are trees of graphical objects. figspec gives the tree
specification-aware font and line defaults while preserving settings
written directly on a child grob. This lets the specification guide the
overall figure without erasing deliberate choices inside individual
elements.

`normalise`` ``<-`` ``function``(``x``)`` ``{`` `` ``(``x`` ``-`` `[`min`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/Extremes.html)`(``x``)``)`` ``/`` `[`diff`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/diff.html)`(`[`range`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/range.html)`(``x``)``)`` ``}`` `` ``grid_figure`` ``<-`` ``grid``::`[`grobTree`](https://rdrr.io/r/grid/grid.grob.html)`(`` `` ``grid``::`[`rectGrob`](https://rdrr.io/r/grid/grid.rect.html)`(`` `` x ``=`` ``0.55``, y ``=`` ``0.5``, width ``=`` ``0.78``, height ``=`` ``0.72``,`` `` gp ``=`` ``grid``::`[`gpar`](https://rdrr.io/r/grid/gpar.html)`(``fill ``=`` ``"#F3F8FC"``, col ``=`` ``"#1A7391"``)`` `` ``)``,`` `` ``grid``::`[`pointsGrob`](https://rdrr.io/r/grid/grid.points.html)`(`` `` x ``=`` ``grid``::`[`unit`](https://rdrr.io/r/grid/unit.html)`(``0.18`` ``+`` ``0.68`` ``*`` ``normalise``(``vehicle_data``$``displ``)``, ``"npc"``)``,`` `` y ``=`` ``grid``::`[`unit`](https://rdrr.io/r/grid/unit.html)`(``0.14`` ``+`` ``0.66`` ``*`` ``normalise``(``vehicle_data``$``hwy``)``, ``"npc"``)``,`` `` pch ``=`` ``21``,`` `` size ``=`` ``grid``::`[`unit`](https://rdrr.io/r/grid/unit.html)`(``2.1``, ``"mm"``)``,`` `` gp ``=`` ``grid``::`[`gpar`](https://rdrr.io/r/grid/gpar.html)`(``fill ``=`` ``"#56B4E9"``, col ``=`` ``"white"``)`` `` ``)``,`` `` ``grid``::`[`textGrob`](https://rdrr.io/r/grid/grid.text.html)`(`` `` ``"Engine size and highway fuel economy"``,`` `` x ``=`` ``0.55``, y ``=`` ``0.91`` `` ``)``,`` `` ``grid``::`[`textGrob`](https://rdrr.io/r/grid/grid.text.html)`(``"Engine displacement"``, x ``=`` ``0.55``, y ``=`` ``0.06``)``,`` `` ``grid``::`[`textGrob`](https://rdrr.io/r/grid/grid.text.html)`(`` `` ``"Highway fuel economy"``,`` `` x ``=`` ``0.08``, y ``=`` ``0.5``, rot ``=`` ``90`` `` ``)`` ``)`` `` ``grid_path`` ``<-`` `[`file.path`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/file.path.html)`(`[`tempdir`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/tempfile.html)`(``)``, ``"figspec-system-grid.png"``)`` ``grid_saved`` ``<-`` `[`fig_save`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/fig_save.md)`(`` `` ``grid_path``,`` `` ``grid_figure``,`` `` spec ``=`` ``figure_spec``,`` `` column ``=`` ``"full"``,`` `` height ``=`` ``75``,`` `` check ``=`` ``FALSE`` ``)`` ``summarise_export``(``grid_saved``)`` ``#> plotting_system requirements_applied canvas_mm`` ``#> 1 grid defaults 110 × 75`

![A grid graphic using real vehicle data, with a pale blue data area and
specification-aware text and line
defaults.](data:image/png;base64,)

Grid trees can have many different internal layouts, so they do not
share one universal data-panel model. Set their complete canvas with
`width` and `height`; figspec then exports and verifies that physical
size.

## Plotly and other HTML widgets

Plotly stores editable layout and trace definitions. figspec can apply
fonts, axis lines, colours, marker symbols, line types and line weights
before export. For a PNG, JPEG or TIFF, it renders the widget in a local
Chrome or Chromium window at the requested pixel dimensions. Nothing is
uploaded to an external service.

`plotly_figure`` ``<-`` ``plotly``::`[`plot_ly`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/plotly/man/plot_ly.html)`(`` `` ``vehicle_data``,`` `` x ``=`` ``~``displ``,`` `` y ``=`` ``~``hwy``,`` `` color ``=`` ``~``drv``,`` `` symbol ``=`` ``~``drv``,`` `` type ``=`` ``"scatter"``,`` `` mode ``=`` ``"markers"`` ``)`` `` ``plotly_saved`` ``<-`` `[`fig_save`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/fig_save.md)`(`` `` ``"plotly-figure.png"``,`` `` ``plotly_figure``,`` `` spec ``=`` ``figure_spec``,`` `` column ``=`` ``"full"``,`` `` height ``=`` ``75`` ``)`

The website build runs that workflow against a real local browser:

![A browser-rendered Plotly scatter plot using the same vehicle data and
project specification as the other
examples.](data:image/png;base64,)

Plotly’s native SVG and PDF export uses its optional Kaleido
environment. Other HTML widgets can be exported to PNG, JPEG or TIFF at
exact dimensions. When a widget exposes additional editable properties,
its adapter can also apply those settings before export.

## Verify the completed files

The plotting systems differ, but the files they produce can be checked
in one way. This example verifies the dimensions, resolution and format
of every file created above:

`exports`` ``<-`` `[`list`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/list.html)`(`` `` ggplot2 ``=`` ``ggplot_saved``,`` `` base_R ``=`` ``base_saved``,`` `` grid ``=`` ``grid_saved`` ``)`` ``if`` ``(`[`exists`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/exists.html)`(``"lattice_saved"``)``)`` ``exports``$``lattice`` ``<-`` ``lattice_saved`` ``if`` ``(`[`exists`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/exists.html)`(``"plotly_saved"``)``)`` ``exports``$``plotly`` ``<-`` ``plotly_saved`` `` ``verification`` ``<-`` `[`lapply`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/lapply.html)`(``exports``, ``function``(``path``)`` ``{`` `` ``report`` ``<-`` `[`fig_check`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/fig_check.md)`(``path``, ``figure_spec``, column ``=`` ``"full"``)`` `` ``report``[`` `` ``report``$``check`` `[`%in%`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/match.html)` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``"Width"``, ``"Resolution"``, ``"File format"``)``,`` `` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``"check"``, ``"actual"``, ``"status"``)`` `` ``]`` ``}``)`` ``verification`` ``#> $ggplot2`` ``#> check actual status`` ``#> 2 Width 109.9 mm pass`` ``#> 4 Resolution 160 dpi pass`` ``#> 5 File format PNG pass`` ``#> `` ``#> $base_R`` ``#> check actual status`` ``#> 2 Width 109.9 mm pass`` ``#> 4 Resolution 160 dpi pass`` ``#> 5 File format PNG pass`` ``#> `` ``#> $grid`` ``#> check actual status`` ``#> 2 Width 109.9 mm pass`` ``#> 4 Resolution 160 dpi pass`` ``#> 5 File format PNG pass`` ``#> `` ``#> $lattice`` ``#> check actual status`` ``#> 2 Width 109.9 mm pass`` ``#> 4 Resolution 160 dpi pass`` ``#> 5 File format PNG pass`` ``#> `` ``#> $plotly`` ``#> check actual status`` ``#> 2 Width 110 mm pass`` ``#> 4 Resolution 160 dpi pass`` ``#> 5 File format PNG pass`

A raster image records pixels, dimensions and resolution, but not the
original point sizes or plotting-system instructions. Check the editable
object for type, layers and mappings, then check the exported file for
its final size, resolution, format and validity.

## Choose the right input

| Figure you have | What to give figspec | What figspec can apply before export | How to complete the workflow |
|----|----|----|----|
| ggplot2 | The plot object | Theme, type, axes, colours, shapes and line rules | Most complete inspection and exact panel sizing |
| patchwork | The composition | Typography across components | Patchwork controls arrangement; exact panel sizing is available |
| base R | A function or one-sided formula containing the drawing code | Device font, type, line and palette defaults | Explicit drawing arguments take precedence |
| lattice | The `trellis` object | Type, colours, symbols, line types and line widths | Exact panel sizing is not available |
| grid | A grob or grob tree | Inherited font and line defaults | Explicit child settings remain unchanged; no general panel model |
| Plotly | The Plotly object | Layout fonts and axes; trace colours, markers and lines | Raster export needs a local browser; vector export needs Kaleido |
| Another HTML widget | The widget object | Exact raster dimensions | Check the rendered file; additional styling depends on the widget’s adapter |
| Recorded base plot | The `recordedplot` | Export without restyling | Check the completed file, or supply the original drawing function to apply defaults |
| Finished file | Its file path | The drawing is already complete | Verify the size, resolution, format and other properties retained by the file |

Use a ggplot2-compatible figure when exact data-panel dimensions or
detailed layer checks are central to the work. For figures built in
another plotting system, figspec provides the same repeatable path from
editable input to a correctly sized and verified file, so the original
plotting system can remain part of the workflow.
